question: An article is marked at ₹550. If it is sold at a discount of 40%, then the selling price becomes 10% more than its cost price. What is the cost price (in ₹)?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Use the direct ratio formula between Cost Price (CP) and Marked Price (MP):

CP : MP = (100 − Discount%) : (100 + Profit%)

CP : MP = (100 − 40) : (100 + 10) = 60 : 110 = 6 : 11

Given MP = 11 units = ₹550 → 1 unit = ₹50

CP = 6 units = 6 × 50 = ₹300

**∴ The correct answer is ₹300.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given: Marked Price (MP) = ₹550, Discount = 40%, Profit = 10%

Formula: Selling Price (SP) = MP × (100 − Discount%)/100; Cost Price (CP) = SP × 100/(100 + Profit%)

 
 CP

 MP = ₹550
 SP = ₹330

⇒ Selling Price (SP) = 550 − (40% of 550)

⇒ SP = 550 − (0.40 × 550)

⇒ SP = 550 − 220 = ₹330

⇒ SP is 10% more than CP → SP = 1.10 × CP

⇒ 330 = 1.10 × CP

⇒ CP = 330 ÷ 1.1 = ₹300

**∴ The correct answer is ₹300.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Marked Price and Selling Price

Marked Price (MP) is the tag price, and the discount is always calculated on this value to reach the Selling Price (SP = MP − Discount).

Effective Percentage Method

If two successive discounts d₁% and d₂% are given, the single equivalent discount is (d₁ + d₂ − (d₁×d₂)/100)%.

Mark-up Percentage

Mark-up is the increase over the CP to set the MP. Mark-up % = [(MP − CP) ÷ CP] × 100.
